<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIIII.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|127 HOLY weeke.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=14|verse=53}}† And they brought {{sc|Iesvs}} to the cheefe Priest: and al the Priests and the Scribes and the Auncients assembled together. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=54}}† And Peter folovved him a farre of euen in vnto the court of the high Priest: and he sate vvith the seruants at the fire, and vvarmed him self. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=55}}† And the cheefe Priests and al the councel sought testimonie against {{sc|Iesvs}}, that they might put him to death, neither found they. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=56}}† For many spake false witnes against him: and the testimonies vvere not cōuenient. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=57}}† And certaine rising vp, bare false vvitnes against him, saying, {{verse|chapter=14|verse=58}}† That vve heard him say, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Io. 2, 19.''}}* I vvil dissolue this temple made vvith hand, and in three daies vvil I build an other not made vvith hand. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=59}}† And their testimonie vvas not conuenient. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=60}}† And the high Priest rising vp into the middes, asked {{sc|Iesvs}}, saying, Ansvverest thou nothing to these things that are obiected to thee of these? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=61}}† But he held his peace and ansvvered nothing. Againe the high Priest asked him, and said to him, Art thou Christ the sonne of the blessed God? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=62}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} saith to him, I am. And you shal see the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Dan. 7, 13.''}}* Sonne of man sitting on the right hand of povver, and comming vvith the cloudes of heauen. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=63}}† And the high Priest renting his garments, saith, VVhat neede vve vvitnesses any further? {{verse|chapter=14|verse=64}}† You haue heard blasphemie. hovv thinke you? VVho al {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Here we may see that they were worthily reprobated and forsaken, according to our Sauiours predictiō by the parable (Mar. 12) The kingdom of God shal be takē from you &c.}}∷ condemned him to be guilty of death. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=65}}† And certaine began to spit vpon him, and to couer his face, and to beate him vvith buffets, and to say vnto him, Prophecie: and the seruants gaue him blovves.

{{verse|chapter=14|verse=66}}† And vvhen Peter vvas in the court beneath, there commeth one of the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ He feareth not afterward Rome the Lady of the world, that in the house of Caiphas was afraid of the high Priestes wench. Leo in Natiu. Pet. & Pau. ser. 1.}}∷ vvoman-seruants of the high Priest. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=67}}† And vvhen she had seen Peter vvarming him self, beholding him she saith, And thou vvast vvith {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=68}}† But he denied, saying, Neither knovv I, neither vvot I vvhat thou saiest. And he vvent forth before the court: and the cocke crevve. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=69}}† And againe a vvench seeing him, began to say to the standers about, That this fellovv is of them. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=70}}† But he denied againe. And after a vvhile againe they that stoode by, said to Peter, Verily thou art of them: for thou art also a Galilæan. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=71}}† But {{sup|‖}} he began to curse and to svveare, That I knovv not this man vvhom you speake of. {{verse|chapter=14|verse=72}}† And immediatly the cocke crevv againe. And Peter remembred the vvord that {{sc|Iesvs}} had said vnto him, Before the cocke crovv tvvise, thou shalt thrise deny me. And he began to vveepe.<noinclude>{{rh|||ANNOT.}}</noinclude>
